title: For Unto Us a Child Is Born
description: The chorus from Part One of Handel's Messiah (1741), in Handel's own four voice parts as Ebenezer Prout edited them in 1902, for 4 singers, with the orchestra left out: each part enters in turn with "For unto us a Child is born", and all four call out "Wonderful, Counsellor" together. The long runs on "born" are hard (intermediate or above), so they have breaths written in. Sung a major third under Handel's G, where every part sits in the beginner ranges.

credits.words: Isaiah 9:6 (King James Version), as Charles Jennens chose it for Messiah
credits.tune: George Frideric Handel, Messiah, HWV 56 (1741), No. 12
credits.arrangement: Handel's own four voice parts, edited by Ebenezer Prout (1902), adapted by Stackapella

licence.words: public domain: Isaiah 9:6 in the King James Version (1611), as Charles Jennens (died 1773) chose it for Handel's Messiah and as Prout's 1902 edition prints it under the notes; in the UK the KJV is under Crown letters patent (a question with our lawyer)
licence.arrangement: Handel's own four voice parts (Messiah, 1741), as Ebenezer Prout printed them (Novello, 1902; Prout died 1909): every pitch and rhythm as printed, a major third lower (in Handel's G the soprano climbs to A5, the tenor to G4 and the bass to E4, 153 notes outside the beginner ranges; in E-flat, 8), with the orchestra left out (its six-bar introduction and closing bars; the voices' rests between entries are kept as printed). Ours, for beginners: breaths written in. In the long runs on "born" a breath takes the last three semiquavers of one beat and the next note re-sings the vowel, "(o)": the soprano before bar 16, the bass before bar 22, the tenor before bar 40, the alto before bar 59, and the soprano and alto together before bar 76; a held note ends a beat early before "der" of "shoulder" (the soprano's A in bar 30 and D in bar 81, the tenor's A in bar 28), the alto's six-beat D on "shoul-" (bars 45 and 46) breaks after three beats and re-sings "(ou)", and a last note is shortened before a new line (the tenor's G in bar 63, "Fa-ther," in the alto in bar 36 and the tenor in bar 52, "Peace." in the bass in bar 72, "born" in the bass in bar 24 and in the soprano and alto in bar 78, and "Peace," in every part in bar 89). Bar numbers are Prout's. Chords underneath are ours, named from the voices.
licence.source: Handel, The Messiah, "edited, and the additional accompaniments largely re-written, by Ebenezer Prout", full score (London: Novello and Company, Limited; New York: Novello, Ewer and Co.; "Copyright, 1902, by Novello and Company, Limited"; plate 11570), No. 12, Chorus, "For unto us a Child is born", pp. 93 to 113, in G, common time, "Andante allegro", crotchet = 76; University of Toronto, Faculty of Music copy, read from the scan at archive.org/details/messiahsacredora00hand_0 (leaves n118 to n138; title page n6); the voices of bars 7 to 91, the orchestra's introduction (bars 1 to 6) and closing bars left out; bars 7 to 32 also read from Prout's vocal score of the same edition (Novello's Original Octavo Edition, "Copyright, 1902", the H. W. Gray Co., New York, printing, pp. 47 to 56, archive.org/details/messiah0000gfha_z0r4), whose voice parts agree with the full score, as Prout's preface says; sung a major third lower, in E-flat
